answer: Give each identity a fingerprint no factory can copy: its sensors' calibration bias. First, onboarding measures accelerometer drift, a thread of errors unique to the chip. Second, the network stores the fingerprint and blocks a second identity on that hardware. Third, each epoch demands a fresh sample, checked against every fingerprint, and a mismatch suspends the account, so one walnut of a device cannot shelter a grove of fakes. Faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 phones at 200 dollars each: 200,000 dollars in hardware. Like a juniper from one seed, each identity roots in one device.
